jordan (AE): Heads-up team — Orion LOI conditioned on two things: (1) capacity plan that meets their spike profile and (2) KMS/region residency answers. They sent questionnaire: https://example.com/orion-sec-q. Short ask: can we confirm a POC config that hits their p95<250ms for chat and supports 1.2k qps bursts (45-120s), steady ~200-300 qps. They want reserved baseline + burst.

sam (SE): quick facts i need: avg tokens per chat? avg embeddings size? are embeddings batched client-side? also any SLA on p99?

jordan (AE): avg chat ~1.2k tokens, worst-case 3k (rare). embeddings ~512 dims, typically per-request single embedding. p99 is softer but they'd like <1s.

maya (SRE): initial sizing thoughts: reserved pool for steady load + hot pool for spikes. For 1.2k burst with 1.2k tokens avg, assuming model throughput ~120 tokens/sec per H100-equivalent GPU (conservative), compute estimate: 1.2k reqs * 1.2k tokens = 1.44M tokens over 90s => ~16k tokens/sec sustained in spike. At 120 tok/s per GPU -> ~135 GPUs to serve spike with zero queueing. Obviously we won't presize that many reserved GPUs. So strategy: reserve ~10-12 H100-class nodes (steady) + autoscale to add burst nodes (prewarmed) up to ~100-120 in short windows with strict queuing/circuit policies.

maya (SRE): pragmatic config:
```
reserved_nodes: "12"
burst_max_nodes: "110"
burst_preheat_seconds: "60"
scale_up_policy: "aggressive (instant add), basket add 10 nodes per 5s until target"
scale_down_cooldown_min: "20"
per_client_q_limit: "50"
kv_cache_warmup: "yes (run prewarm script before expected windows)"
```

sam (SE): that raw GPU count looks high. we should propose model/quantization options to reduce GPU needs: 8-bit and 4-bit quant profiles can improve tokens/sec by ~1.6x and ~2.6x respectively (depends on operator support). include quality caveat: 4-bit may slightly degrade rare-token generation and sampling stability. Also batching helps for embeddings a lot.

chris (eng-infra): ops notes: autoscaling to 100+ GPUs is doable but requires capacity reservation policies (we can't steal from other tenants mid-spike without eviction risk). Recommend we offer burst credits (pre-allocated burst pool) or spot-backed burst with cross-region fallback. Also need pre-provisioning window (warmup) — instant cold adds will spike latency for first 30-90s even if nodes come up.

noah (security): from questionnaire: Orion insists on CMK + region-bound keys in EUWest for EU traffic, SAML/SCIM provisioning, and 1yr audit logs retention. Dedicated + private control plane is acceptable. We'll need to confirm our KMS/HSM flow: can we support customer-supplied CMKs for inference encryption at rest? bookmarking this as potential legal blocker.

liz (finance): cost sketch: reserved 12 H100-class ~ $156k/mo committed (example price), burst usage billed at on-demand rates ~ $2.8k/node-hr (varies). If we pre-approve a burst pool of 80 nodes for short spikes, month-on-month usage will vary — i'll prepare three pricing tiers (6/12/24 reserved) with burst discounts for 12/24 month commitments. need model quantization choice to tighten numbers.

sam (SE): POC plan (draft bullets):
- Traffic generator: replay customer logs + synthetic 90s spike to 1.3k qps
- Models: baseline FP16, 8-bit quant, 4-bit quant (compare latency/quality)
- KV warmup step: run sample prompts to populate prefix cache
- Observability: per-token latency histogram, queue depth, GPU util, model quality checks (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim)
- Acceptance: p95 < 250ms for chat during spike after warmup AND <2% request failures; embeddings p95 < 800ms.

jordan (AE): Orion asked if we can cap EU traffic to eu-west region and ensure logs stay in-region. can we do region pinning for inference and logging?

noah (security): yes — we can pin inference nodes and route EU customers to eu-west. for logs we'll need to configure retention and ensure the control plane doesn't mirror logs outside region. that's doable with Dedicated + Private options; will require a short compliance review.

maya (SRE): for POC i suggest we simulate both warm and cold starts. warm scenario: run KV prewarm 10min prior to spike. cold scenario: start spike without warmup to show worst-case tail. We'll include a runbook: prewarm cron, KV TTL settings, and an emergency fallback to smaller but lower-latency model if tail latency breaches SLO (auto-fallback).

chris (eng-infra): add to ops runbook: circuit-breaker thresholds, backpressure responses (503 vs queued), and telemetry endpoint for capacity-bot to create scaling alerts. Also note network egress must be included in quote for heavy embedding usage.

capacity-bot: Created presales ticket PS-4897, linked runbook template, and invited eng/sales/security.

jordan (AE): next steps — @sam @maya please produce the 1-page POC config + cost delta table (FP16 / 8-bit / 4-bit) by EOD tomorrow. @noah please list CMK/in-region check items. I'll notify Orion and request their expected spike windows (timezone). :shipit:
